subject: POC trial planning: workload intake & success criteria (AcmeHealth)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning: workload intake & success criteria (AcmeHealth)

Hi Alex / Sophie —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff:

Summary of what we covered:
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for clinical-annotated note summarization and triage workflows (privacy/compliance still in scope).
- High-level success criteria (please confirm):
  - P95 latency for end-to-end generation <= 300ms for single-request flows
  - Throughput target: sustain production baseline RPS with acceptable tail latency (see workload ask below)
  - Cost/quality: model outputs meet your QA pass rate on the evaluation set (>= 95% acceptance by clinical reviewer)

Evaluation plan & timeline (proposed):
- May 6: 60–90min engineering workshop (schema, auth, network, data sanitization) — owners: Ben (AE), Marissa (SRE/SE), Alex (Acme eng)
- May 10–12: Baseline perf tests with synthetic traffic and your eval dataset
- May 15–Jun 15: 4-week POC (integration + production-like load testing)

Workload intake needed (attached spreadsheet: acme_workload_profile.xlsx): please fill the fields below so we can size the environment and create realistic test harnesses:
- Baseline RPS (average sustained)
- Peak burst RPS and typical burst duration
- Typical input/output token lengths (avg/min/max)
- Expected concurrency (# of concurrent sessions) and burst patterns (time-of-day, day-of-week)
- Percentage of requests that use long-context (10%+ with >2k tokens)
- Any hard SLOs by route/type (e.g., triage = 200ms p95)

Attachments: redwood_poc-template.pdf (POC checklist), acme_workload_profile.xlsx (intake sheet).

Please send the filled intake sheet back by EOD Tue (May 3) if possible — we can still proceed without all fields but the more detail we have the better tuned the POC will be.

Thanks — I’ll block time for the May 6 workshop and send calendar invites once I hear availability.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acmehealth.com>, Michael Brown <michael.brown@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning: workload intake & success criteria (AcmeHealth)

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Attached is the filled workload intake (acme_workload_profile-filled.xlsx). Key items called out below for your sizing and test plan:

Workload summary (production expected):
- Baseline RPS (avg sustained): 5 requests/sec
- Peak burst RPS: up to 50 requests/sec for 2–5 minutes (typically morning batch processing 8:00–9:00 PDT)
- Concurrency: typical 20 concurrent sessions with spikes to 100 for short windows (30–300s)
- Input tokens (clinical notes trim): avg 120 tokens, 90% range 40–300
- Output tokens (summaries + metadata): avg 450 tokens, 90% range 150–1,200
- Long-context usage: ~8% of requests include appended patient history pushing total tokens to 3k–6k

Evaluation dataset: we will provide a redacted set of ~5k documents for QA scoring. Primary eval metrics: QA acceptance rate (>=95%), semantic fidelity checks, and p95 latency.

Compliance note: all data is redacted for the POC; production will require our SOC2 + signed DPA (we have procurement on standby).

Let us know if you need traffic traces or a synthetic generator. Plan works for us — Alex / Sophie can do May 6 workshop (prefer morning PST).

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Senior Engineering Manager, AcmeHealth
alex.johnson@acmehealth.com

Attachments: acme_workload_profile-filled.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: AcmeHealth POC workload notes

Thanks Alex for the details — copying my internal notes so we have a concrete plan for infra sizing and test config:

Notes / recommendations:
- Given baseline 5 RPS + 50RPS bursts and concurrency spikes, recommend small Dedicated pool (2x A100 equiv) with autoscale thresholds: scale up at 20 concurrent, scale down after 10m idle.
- Enable KV caching for repeated prefixes (clinical templates) to reduce token compute for summaries; we should estimate cache hit rate after initial tests (Marissa to own).
- For long-context (3k–6k tokens) sequences, we should test both full attention and chunked-context handling — schedule an engineer to validate memory/latency trade-offs (Dylan to run mem/latency matrix).
- Quantization: try 4-bit int8/4-bit mix where supported; we may recommend 4-bit fused kernels for cost QA runs.
- Synthetic load generator: create a mix with 70% short sessions (<=600 output tokens), 22% medium, 8% long-context sessions — will mirror Alex's distribution.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: create perf matrix and recommend Dedicated sizing by May 5
- Dylan: build synthetic generator and run baseline perf May 10–12
- Ben: schedule May 6 workshop and confirm calendar with Acme

I’ll draft a short runbook for the May 10 baseline tests we can share with Acme.

-Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning: workload intake & success criteria (AcmeHealth)

Alex — really helpful, thanks for the fast turnaround and the filled sheet. Quick follow-up / confirmation:

Confirmed items:
- May 6 workshop: proposed 9:00–10:30 PDT — Marissa + Dylan + I will join. Please confirm calendar invite.
- Baseline perf window: May 10–12 (Dylan will run synthetic + a small subset of your redacted data)
- Full POC: May 15–Jun 15 (integration + production-like stress tests)

Success criteria for POC (please confirm):
1) QA acceptance >= 95% on provided eval set by clinical reviewers
2) p95 latency <= 300ms for the majority (>=90%) of short/medium flows; note: long-context flows expected to have higher latency — we will track separately
3) No severe reliability incidents during 72h sustained runs at baseline + two scheduled burst events

If these criteria look good, please reply with a one-line sign-off. Also confirm whether procurement needs a SOW or if the standard POC template is sufficient.

Next steps when confirmed:
- I’ll send the May 6 calendar invite and the Zoom link
- Marissa and Dylan will send the perf/runbook and synthetic generator repo link

Thanks — looking forward to kicking this off.

-Ben

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>

Ben — sign-off below and confirm we’re on the same page.

One-line sign-off: AcmeHealth approves the proposed success criteria and POC timeline (May 15–Jun 15); we will provide the redacted eval dataset by May 7.

Procurement: SOW not required for the initial POC; the standard POC template is sufficient — we’ll handle DPA/SOC2 in parallel.

We’ve attached the filled intake and added an example trace file. Happy to meet May 6 at 9:00 PDT.

—Alex
